result.summary: This pull request assigns mapped autonomous systems a distinct network group tag to prevent address group collisions with unmapped IPv6 /32 prefixes. It updates the peer bucketing format version so ASMap nodes rebucket stored addresses across upgrades and downgrades. Additionally, it fixes an issue where digit-leading filenames passed to `-asmap` were treated as boolean true, prevents `exportasmap` from overwriting existing files, and refines startup error handling for invalid map paths.
result.problem: Mapped AS numbers currently share the IPv6 group tag, causing nodes to conflate mapped autonomous systems with unmapped IPv6 /32 subnets and treat unrelated peers as belonging to the same address group when selecting connections or bucketing peers. In addition, setting `-asmap` to a filename starting with digits (such as `2026-09-asmap.dat`) caused argument parsing to interpret it as a boolean, silently using the embedded map instead of loading the user's file. Finally, `exportasmap` could silently overwrite an existing custom map on disk.
evidence: PR description: 'A mapped autonomous system and an unmapped IPv6 /32 can share an address group, so the node treats unrelated peers as part of the same network when selecting connections.'
PR description and commit 81a507ab75: 'Reading `-asmap` as a boolean made a filename such as `2026-09-asmap.dat` select the embedded map.'

Commit 119cf8b050: 'With `-asmap=asmap.dat`, running `exportasmap asmap.dat` replaces the configured map on disk with the embedded one. The running node keeps using the custom map until its next restart.'
result.scope_notes: The author notes that multiple unrelated ASMap fixes are batched together across initialization, P2P netgroup bucketing, RPC, and documentation, and can be split if reviewers prefer.
result.card: This pull request gives ASMap autonomous systems their own network group tag so mapped peers do not collide with unmapped IPv6 /32 subnets, rebucketing peers.dat addresses for ASMap users on upgrade. It also fixes an argument-parsing bug where digit-leading filenames like 2026-09-asmap.dat were interpreted as boolean true and silently fell back to the embedded map. Furthermore, it protects against accidental file destruction by preventing exportasmap from overwriting existing files and cleans up startup validation of map paths. Batched together across net, init, and RPC, these fixes prevent improper peer diversification and map configuration errors.
uncertainties: The full patch diff was not provided in the prompt, limiting inspection to commit messages and PR metadata.

risk.why: Mistakes in address group tagging or peer rebucketing could degrade connection diversity or corrupt peers.dat serialization across restarts.
